general_rules.description: Internal team (same domain) receives casual tone with no greeting or first-name-only greetings, no closing signature.
Code-switching with French colleagues: mix English and French in same email, use 'tu' form, casual emoji (👌, 🔥, 🙏).
External French contacts (clients, investors, government) receive formal French with 'vous', 'Bonjour' greeting, and 'Bien cordialement,' closing with full signature.
Investor/VC contacts (Marcus, Sarah) receive semi-formal to formal English with 'Hi' greeting and first name only as closing, emoji used sparingly (💪, 🚀).
Action-oriented emails to internal team use imperative mood, numbered lists, and emoji for emphasis (⚠️, 🚀, ✅).
Data-heavy emails to investors include structured bullet points, metrics, and financial figures with professional formatting.
French formal emails include full signature block with title (CEO - HeyVibe) and company details.
Casual internal emails omit signature entirely and use ultra-short closings or none at all.
